pages.title: What this extension does
pages.explains: Location adds a page that shows where this device is and, on a drawn map, where the paired devices that shared their location with it were, how far away and in which direction. This device is in the middle of the map when it knows where it is; otherwise one of the devices that shared with it is. It asks your system where this device is only when you press a button on the page (or, if you turn it on, every five minutes while the page is open), and sends that position only to the paired devices you allowed.
pages.changes: After installing, Location appears among the pages. To find this device it needs the permission to know where this device is; your system may also ask you once. To share, it needs, for each paired device, the permissions to see it, to send to it and to share locations with it, and Location must be installed and allowed for this device on the other one too. Received locations are kept in memory only and are forgotten when the application stops, when you press Forget, or as soon as you unpair that device or stop allowing Location for it.

body.text: What is sent, and to whom

items: Only when you share. Pressing Share my location sends this device's position once; Keep sharing sends it again every five minutes while the page is open, and stops when you turn it off or leave the page.
Only to devices you allowed. A paired device receives it only if you allowed Location for it here, and its own person allowed Location for this device there.

Only the position. Latitude, longitude, how sure your system was and how old the fix is: no name, address, history or anything else. It travels straight between the two devices, through the application's encrypted connection; Location sends nothing anywhere else.
How your system finds it is your system's own. Satellites, or the wireless networks it sees, which your system may look up with an online service of its own; Location receives only the position.
